data.title: Media Property Created to Carry the Narrative
data.summary:
Websites presenting as independent news or research outlets were created to publish
campaign content, giving the claims a citable source outside social platforms.
data.description:
An owned outlet converts an assertion into a citation. Social posts can then link to
"reporting" rather than to each other, the content survives platform enforcement because
it lives on infrastructure the operator controls, and search engines index it as a source.

These properties are usually identifiable: thin or generated staff pages, no corrections
policy, no physical address, hosting and registration shared with other campaign assets,
and a publication history that begins shortly before the campaign. The shared
infrastructure is the most productive thread, since one property frequently exposes a
network of them.

Where the outlet's name or design imitates a real publication, that is a separate and
more actionable finding, since the imitated publication has standing to act.
data.recommendation:
* Map hosting, registration and analytics identifiers across properties; they commonly
  reveal the wider network.
* Notify any genuine publication being imitated, as it can act where the client cannot.
* Report the properties to search engines and to hosting providers under their policies
  rather than only to social platforms.
data.short_recommendation: Map shared hosting and registration; notify any imitated publication.
